children: DRDO highlights next-generation chip design, AI system-on-chips and domestic technology development at ESTIC 2026

India aims to become a globally competitive, technologically self-reliant semiconductor powerhouse by 2047, focusing on indigenous chip development, stronger domestic capabilities, and resilient supply chains, the Defence Ministry said on Friday.
The vision includes establishing a sustainable semiconductor ecosystem, creating high-value employment opportunities and developing expertise in selected next-generation chip technologies.
The ministry said semiconductors would be central to India's ambitions of achieving technological sovereignty, economic strength and digital security under the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.
The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) highlighted these priorities during the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026.

As one of the key organisers of the conclave, DRDO led a thematic session on 'Semiconductors and Next-Generation Chips', chaired by B K Das, Director General of Electronics and Communication Systems (ECS).
The session brought together representatives from industry, academia, the indigenous chip-development ecosystem and defence electronics to discuss emerging semiconductor technologies.
Discussions covered purpose-built artificial intelligence (AI) system-on-chips (SoCs), intelligence at the silicon edge and developments in microprocessor technologies.

The discussions also examined DRDO's role in supporting industries and startups in developing advanced chip designs, accelerating next-generation technology development and strengthening indigenous semiconductor capabilities.

The ministry highlighted that semiconductor self-reliance would require capabilities extending beyond chip manufacturing to include design, fabrication, testing, industrial-scale production and resilient supply chains.
The DRDO's outreach stall at the conclave featured technologies and research programmes developed by its laboratories across defence and strategic sectors.

The exhibits included advanced communication systems, quantum technology prototypes, extreme-cold-weather clothing, the PRABALA female full-body protector, passive and powered exoskeletons, portable hybrid energy management systems, high-power pulse laser diodes and scramjet engine technology.

The ministry said the development of indigenous semiconductor capabilities would contribute to the government's broader vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 and strengthen the country's pursuit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat through greater technological self-reliance.
